title: Answer to Question: The Repercussions of the Greek Crisis
text:
Answer to Question

The Repercussions of the Greek Crisis

Question:

The news reported on Friday 27/2/2015 that the German parliament had approved by an overwhelming majority the extension of aid to Greece for four months... So does this mean that the Greek crisis has ended, and that Greece will continue as a member of the European Union without obstacles? Furthermore, it has been noticed that America is concerned that Greece remains in the European Union and that its problems are solved, for Obama declared during the height of the crisis, in an interview with CNN on 1/2/2015, expressing "his hope that Greece remains in the eurozone," and he mentioned that "this requires compromises from all sides," and he said "the best way to reduce the deficit and restore robustness lies in achieving growth." So what is the motive for this open intervention by America in the crisis of Greece? And may Allah reward you with good.

Answer:

So that the picture becomes clear, we will review the following matters:

1- The latest financial crisis of Greece began to appear at the end of 2009, after the global financial crisis exploded in America, the head of capitalism, and encompassed Europe and the rest of the world that is subject to the capitalist system. It struck Greece in April 2010, and following that, on 23/6/2010, the Greek government officially requested the European Union and the International Monetary Fund to activate a rescue plan including loans to help Greece avoid bankruptcy and default on its debts. The interest rates on Greek bonds rose, as did the insurance on these bonds against default; all of that rose to high rates as a result of investors' fears of "Greece's inability to meet its debts, with the rise in the budget deficit rate and the escalation of the volume of public debt, in addition to the weakness of growth in the Greek economy." This crisis threatened the situation of the euro and its zone, and consequently the European Union as a whole, and the idea of Greece's exit from this economic zone was raised. However, Europe decided to provide aid to Greece in return for its implementing economic reforms and austerity measures aimed at reducing the deficit in the general budget. This is bearing in mind that the current programme of so-called reforms was due to end on 28 February of the current month. The agreement was not decisive in its content, but it postponed the explosion, as was said.

2- The package provided to Greece over 5 years is estimated at 240 billion euros, while the Greek debt has currently reached 323 billion euros, divided as follows: 60% of these debts are owed to the eurozone, 10% to the International Monetary Fund, 6% to the European Central Bank, 4% to Greek banks, 1% to foreign banks, 1% to the Greek central bank, 3% other loans, and 15% treasury bonds. The Eurogroup stipulates achieving a budget surplus of 3% after paying the interest on the loans. Greece does not have the ability to achieve that, but the Greek finance minister says that his country is no longer bound by this condition according to the latest agreement, while Germany and the group have not issued any clarification on this matter. The austerity policy imposed on Greece in recent years has led to a continuous state of economic recession during the past years, a rise in the unemployment rate to 27% and the bankruptcy of about one third of private enterprises. Greece has been living since 2010 under the austerity programme, and of the European financial rescue to service its debts, more than 200 billion euros of the loans provided so far have gone to rescuing the banks and hedge funds that are creditors of Greece, foremost among them the French and German banks. These loans were provided by the European Union, the International Monetary Fund and the European Central Bank in return for Greece's commitment to austerity measures. That is, the European Union pays its banks that lent to Greece at high usurious interest (riba), at a time when the Greek citizen has lost confidence in his country's economy; for example, 18 billion euros have been withdrawn since last December, and 500 million were withdrawn on the 18th and 19th of the current month. All of this indicates the corruption and danger of what are called capitalist rescue plans, for they are drowning and not rescuing, and destructive to the lands and the people...

3- Germany was the most hardline of the states on the issue of the Greek crisis and refuses to exempt it from the debts. Therefore Germany was at the head of the negotiators and led the talks, so much so that they were described as talks between Germany and Greece. Accordingly, the news reported that the agreement was not reached through real negotiations between the ministers of the 19 states of the eurozone and Greece, but rather through negotiations between the German finance minister and his Greek counterpart in the presence of officials from the International Monetary Fund and the European Central Bank. This allowed the anti-European Union current in Britain to intensify its criticism of the bloc as a club controlled by Germany, through which it seeks to control Europe. Germany has begun to feel that it is the financial leader of the European Union because it is the strongest European economic state, and everyone stretches out his hand to it and shows his need for it and for its help. And Germany does not want to be lenient on the issue of the Greek crisis, because the contagion would move to Portugal as a first stage, and at a later stage to Ireland, Italy, Spain and other states of the Union that suffer from similar problems. These states are subject to the rescue programme and apply the austerity policy that Germany imposed in the name of the Union. If Germany were lenient with Greece, those states would begin to abandon the austerity policy that burdens the shoulders of their citizens. Therefore the German finance minister Wolfgang Schäuble, who is among the fiercest opponents of the idea of exempting Greece from the debts, said: "Greece will not obtain aid before implementing the conditions stipulated by the current agreement," and he said: "The government led by the socialists is going through difficult times" (BBC, 21/2/2015). And the spokesman of the Greek government, Panagiotis Agravitos, said "that Greece and Germany have reached an agreement on extending the programme of rescue loans to Greece for 4 months, and he said there is an agreement regarding the partner institutions, Greece and Germany" (Al-Quds, 20/2/2015). Finally, after the Greek government pledged to commit to the programme without any reservation or conditions, the European parliament, or rather the German parliament, approved on 27/2/2015 the extension of the deadline for a period of four months... And Schäuble affirmed that the current agreement "will not include paying new billions to Greece nor does it contain any changes to the current programme" (Al-Arab, London, 28/2/2015). And Schäuble sought to reassure that the matter does not at all concern "granting new billions to Greece" or amending the conditions of the current programme. And the European Commissioner for Economic Affairs, Pierre Moscovici, urged Athens to "respect its commitments towards its European partners and the International Monetary Fund" (swissinfo.ch - afp_tickers, 27/2/2015).

4- As for the position of France, which is the main state in the European Union alongside Germany, the French President François Hollande described the agreement as "a good settlement for both Greece and its lenders" (BBC, 21/2/2015). And the French finance minister Michel Sapin said "that Athens ultimately agreed to remain under the supervision of the creditor parties, but there will be work of another nature; there will certainly be political work," indicating that the Greeks no longer want to meet technicians (Agence France-Presse, 21/2/2015). And the agency added: "If Greece fulfils its conditions, it will obtain up to 2.7 billion dollars of the remaining funds of the European financing within the framework of the rescue deal amounting to 240 billion euros. Greece is keen to turn the page on austerity, but Germany, the guarantor of strictness in budgets in Europe, has stipulated that Greece continue cleaning up its finances and proceed with structural reforms."

5- As for the position of America, its open intervention in the matter was clear. The American President Barack Obama declared in an interview with CNN on 1/2/2015, commenting on the financial crisis in Greece, standing on its side and criticising the European Union's position towards it, saying: "You cannot keep on squeezing countries that are in the midst of depression," and he added: "At some point there has to be a growth strategy in order for them to pay off their debts." He acknowledged that "there is an urgent need for Greece to carry out reforms," but he said: "It is very hard to initiate these changes if people's standard of living has dropped by 25%. Over time, the political system and society cannot sustain that." And Obama expressed "his hope that Greece remains in the eurozone," and mentioned that "this requires compromises from all sides." And he criticised the European austerity policy, saying: "When an economy is in continuous decline, there has to be a growth strategy, and not just efforts to further squeeze a population that is hurting more and more." And he said: "The best way to reduce the deficit and restore robustness lies in achieving growth." The American President's words came several days after the victory of the leftist Syriza party in the Greek legislative elections held on 25/1/2015, and about a month before the end of the European rescue phase for Greece, to give a clear signal to Europe that he stands on Greece's side and criticises Europe, so as to pressure it to keep Greece within the European Union, and to exploit his backing of it against the Union. For America wants Greece to remain inside the European Union so that this Union continues to suffer from crises and cracks and remains a fragile union threatened with collapse.

6- As for Greece itself, where a leftist government led by the Syriza party came to power a month ago, it wants to remain in the European Union. The Greek Prime Minister Alexis Tsipras praised the agreement, saying: "His government foiled a plan by conservative forces in Greece and abroad to bankrupt the country at the end of the month," i.e., the date of the expiry of the European rescue deal. And he added: "The agreement with the leaders of the European Union on a four-month extension for Greece will end the hated austerity measures in the country. However, the government still faces difficult challenges." And he said, claiming, "that the agreement cancels austerity." However, this agreement came in return for making concessions, among them its commitment to specifying the so-called reforms within two days. And he said "that his government will focus on negotiating new reforms with the donors by June" (AFP, 21/2/2015). The Greek government had requested the extension of Greece's financing for 6 months so that it could present reform plans for a period of four years. And the Greek government said that it avoided large cuts to pensions, as well as avoiding raising taxes significantly, and that it convinced the European creditors to abandon their unrealistic demands concerning the budget. And the Greek finance minister considered the agreement a first step on a long road, and he added, saying: "No one can impose on our economy and our society measures that we do not agree on, and this is the new thing in the agreement. We now have a new framework, but we respect what preceded. Now we have pledged to participate in writing these reforms, for which we will be held accountable." For his part, the German finance minister Wolfgang Schäuble said: "As long as the programme with Greece has not been successfully agreed upon, there will be no money, and this is clear" (Euronews, 21/2/2015). That was before Greece agreed to the conditions of the programme and then Germany agreed to the extension.

7- As for the British position, the British finance minister George Osborne described the current situation in Greece's dispute with other partners in the eurozone as "representing a risk to the stability of the British economy, and he demanded that the euro states must reach a common solution so that they can repel an escalating crisis." And he said: "In this difficult situation lie the risks of a crisis that could lead to great damage to the European economy, and it also represents a risk for Britain" (Sky News, 20/2/2015). Britain wants the European Union to remain in existence as long as it benefits from it and it does not constitute a danger to it. Especially as the whole Western world is suffering from an aggravated financial crisis, and the collapse of the European Union at this time would deal a blow that might be fatal to the capitalist economy as a whole. And it, i.e., Britain, wants the European Union to remain in existence competing with America, so that it can use it in its hidden struggle with America and prevent the latter from monopolising the politics of the world.

8- We conclude from all of this the following:

a- The European Union is a fragile union, because it is not built upon the unity of political decision, and it is not a single political entity. There is no single central administration that runs it; rather, it is a group of states that agree in some places and positions and differ in others, and its major powers compete among themselves over its leadership and over imposing their will upon it, especially if we know that it is based on utilitarianism, due to its adoption of the capitalist ideology which makes benefit the basis and the measure of actions, and that they are nationalist states seeking to achieve sovereignty over others, because this ideology endorsed nationalism and did not treat it, so it could not merge the peoples who believe in it into a single melting pot. The European states, especially the major ones, compete among themselves for sovereignty over the states of the Union: Germany seeks to achieve that, France seeks a prominent role as a partner to Germany, and Britain seeks to use the Union to compete with America in such a way that it benefits from both sides.

b- America tries to penetrate the states of the Union and influence them, and it works to strike it and works to undermine it, lest it become a single political unity with globally influential power, and so that the euro falls, so that no global currency remains competing with its currency, the dollar. America exploits the crises and problems of the Union and faults its treatments, in order to lower its standing and so that it remains the leader of the capitalist world without a competitor. So it exploited the crisis of Greece, and it is working to flirt with the leftist government there and to attract it to itself, and it defends its remaining in the Union so that it remains fragile, gnawed at by crises. It will work to exploit it and encourage it to take positions in the face of the European Union, so that Greece becomes a factor of weakness or cracking for the Union, and thus the Union comes to face the danger of collapse.

c- Germany works to preserve the Union and the Eurogroup and strengthen them, and it has almost become the holder of the first word in them. It is the first beneficiary, for its financial institutions are the ones that benefit: it lends to Greece and the other European states and recovers these funds with profits, thereby moving the wheel of the economy in its financial institutions of banks, reserve funds and insurance companies. And it works to strengthen its influence in it. It has now come to be described as a medium major state globally. France is the second beneficiary in the same manner as Germany, and it works to strengthen its international role through the Union. There remains Britain, which watches the situation as if it were not a member of it; it neither works to strengthen it nor seeks to bring it down, but rather works to benefit from it and harness it.

d- Thus the competition will remain present between the major states in the Union, and the struggle will remain present between the Union and America, which seeks to undermine it and fragment it if it is able to do so, and seeks to bring down the euro as a global currency, so that it keeps its green paper, which is not worth the ink it was printed with, as a global currency with which it plunders the wealth of the world and finances its military machine to guarantee its global sovereignty as the first state controlling the world.

e- Thus it is proven, time after time, that capitalism is a false ideology, its economic system is corrupt, its treatments are dangerous and its results are disastrous. It does not treat the diseases, but rather works to sedate them, so the problems remain present and the diseases chronic. The riba (usury) which it adopts as a basis in transactions and debts is destructive and weighs down the shoulders of the debtor. In addition to that, the borrowing state that issues treasury bonds to borrow with riba must insure these bonds, so it pays other enormous sums for the insurance. Thus the burdens on the borrowing state increase and that does not rescue it; rather, it continues to suffer from deficit in the budget and in the ability to repay the debt, and it keeps it under the control of the creditors! And it keeps its citizens living in hardship and a wretched life as a result of forcing it to apply the austerity policy. Greece, around which the talk is taking place, is the most prominent example of that, for all the treatments of its crisis, as shown above, are at best painkillers for a period, then before long it explodes, and so on... bearing in mind that Greece lived for a period of four centuries in ease of living, stability, security and safety under the rule of Islam.
